proof:
Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

Source: Step 2 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Remark 3.12 (p. 149: the codimension-0 case "is a direct consequence of Remark 2.35 and the Compactness Theorem for BV functions (§2.6 of Ch. 2)"), with 2.35 specialized to integer multiplicity currents. Book n = m + 1 = P. (Only integrality of the T_j themselves is needed, not of ∂T_j; this is how the result is also used in Step 11(iv) of the parent proof.)

Notation. n := m + 1, ℝⁿ = Eucl n with standard basis e = (e_1,…,e_n); E := simpleNVector e = e_1∧⋯∧e_n; dx := dx^{(1,…,n)}, the n-covector with dx(e) = 1. Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure Lⁿ on ℝⁿ.

1. (Top-degree forms.) Λⁿ(ℝⁿ)* is one-dimensional: every n-covector is α = α(e)·dx, and |α| = |α(e)| (I(n,n) has one element). So every ω ∈ D^n(U) is ω = a·dx with a := ω(·)(e) ∈ C_c^∞(U) and ‖ω‖ = sup|a|. For (n−1)-forms, the increasing (n−1)-tuples are I_i := (1,…,î,…,n), i = 1,…,n; write ω = Σ_i ω_i dx^{(i)} with dx^{(i)} := dx^{I_i}; then |ω|² = Σ_i ω_i², and dω = Σ_i (−1)^{i−1} (D_iω_i) dx.
2. (Densities of the T_j.) Write T_j = τ(M_j,θ_j,ξ_j) (i.m.). For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_j, ξ_j(x) = ±simpleNVector τ with τ an orthonormal n-frame of ℝⁿ, and simpleNVector τ = det[τ]·E with det[τ] = ±1 (alternating multilinearity; τ = e·[τ] with [τ] orthogonal). Hence ξ_j = σ_j E a.e. on M_j with σ_j := ξ_j(dx) ∈ {±1} measurable. Put β_j := 1_{M_j} θ_j σ_j: integer valued, measurable, and locally Lⁿ-integrable in U (|β_j| = 1_{M_j}θ_j is integrable on compact subsets of U). Then for ω = a dx: T_j(ω) = ∫_{M_j} θ_j ξ_j(a(x) dx) dLⁿ = ∫_U a β_j dLⁿ.
3. (Masses; Remark 2.35 in the i.m. case.) For open W ⊆ U:
   (i) ∫_W |β_j| dLⁿ ≤ M_W(T_j): given a compact K ⊆ W and ε > 0, by Lusin's theorem and mollification there is a ∈ C_c^∞(W) with |a| ≤ 1 and ∫_W |a − sign(β_j)1_K| |β_j| dLⁿ < ε; then T_j(a dx) ≥ ∫_K |β_j| − ε; let ε → 0 and K ↑ W.
   (ii) M_W(∂T_j) = |Dβ_j|(W) := sup{∫ β_j div g dLⁿ : g ∈ C_c^∞(W;ℝⁿ), |g| ≤ 1}: for ω = Σ_iω_i dx^{(i)} ∈ D^{n−1}(U) with tsupport ⊆ W, ∂T_j(ω) = T_j(dω) = ∫ β_j Σ_i(−1)^{i−1}D_iω_i dLⁿ = ∫ β_j div g dLⁿ with g_i := (−1)^{i−1}ω_i, and |ω| = |g| pointwise (step 1); ω ↦ g is a bijection between admissible forms and admissible fields (Simon Ch. 2, 2.4 allows smooth g as well).
   Hence for every W ⊂⊂ U: sup_j (∫_W|β_j| dLⁿ + |Dβ_j|(W)) ≤ sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ by hypothesis; in particular β_j ∈ BV_loc(U).
4. (BV compactness.) By the Compactness Theorem for BV functions (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6) there are a subsequence (j′) and β ∈ BV_loc(U) with β_{j′} → β in L¹_loc(U). Choosing an exhaustion W_1 ⊂⊂ W_2 ⊂⊂ ⋯ of U (e.g. W_l := {x ∈ U : |x| < l, dist(x, ℝⁿ∖U) > 1/l}) and a diagonal subsequence, β_{j′} → β Lⁿ-a.e. on U. At such a point x the sequence of integers β_{j′}(x) converges, hence is eventually constant, so β(x) ∈ ℤ. Fix a Borel representative β : ℝⁿ → ℤ of this limit with β = 0 outside U.
5. (Identification of T.) For ω = a dx ∈ D^n(U), choose l with spt a ⊆ W_l; then T(ω) = lim_{j′} T_{j′}(ω) = lim ∫ a β_{j′} dLⁿ = ∫ a β dLⁿ, since |∫ a(β_{j′} − β)| ≤ sup|a| ∫_{W_l} |β_{j′} − β| → 0.
6. (T is i.m.) Let M := {x ∈ U : β(x) ≠ 0} (Borel), θ := |β| (θ := 1 off M), ξ := sign(β)·E on M (ξ := E off M). Then τ(M,θ,ξ)(a dx) = ∫_M |β| sign(β) a dLⁿ = ∫ a β dLⁿ = T(a dx), and θ ∈ {1,2,…} on M. IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ:
   - M ⊆ U; M is Borel, hence null-measurable;
   - M is countably n-rectifiable: M ⊆ ℝⁿ = range(id), id Lipschitz;
   - θ > 0 on M, and θ is integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U (β ∈ L¹_loc(U));
   - ξ is measurable (two values on Borel pieces);
   - orients: let x ∈ M be a Lebesgue point of β, i.e. r^{−n} ∫_{B̄_r(x)} |β(z) − β(x)| dLⁿ(z) → 0 (Lⁿ-a.e. x, by Lebesgue's differentiation theorem; Lⁿ(B̄_r) = ω_n rⁿ). Take τ := e (orthonormal, span τ = ℝⁿ). Apply `iwl_weighted_tangent_locality` to (M, θ) and (M′, θ′) := (ℝⁿ, the constant function c := |β(x)|) at x: M is Borel and ℝⁿ is measurable (so both are Hⁿ-null-measurable); θ(x) = c = θ′(x); choosing ρ > 0 with B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ U, θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and the constant c on B̄_ρ(x); and since 1_M|β| = |β| everywhere (β = 0 off M), for every R > 0
     r^{−n} ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |1_Mθ − c| dLⁿ = r^{−n} ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} ||β| − |β(x)|| dLⁿ ≤ Rⁿ (Rr)^{−n} ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |β − β(x)| dLⁿ → 0.
     Moreover HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n ℝⁿ c x ℝⁿ holds: dim ℝⁿ = n, and η_{x,r}(ℝⁿ) = ℝⁿ, so ∫_{η_{x,r}(ℝⁿ)} f(y) c dHⁿ(y) = c ∫_{ℝⁿ} f dHⁿ for every r > 0, which is the required limit. Hence HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (span e), and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector e.
   Therefore T = τ(M,θ,ξ) is integer multiplicity. ∎
key_steps: An integer multiplicity n-current in U ⊆ ℝⁿ is [[U]]⌞β_j with β_j integer valued, since the orientation is ±e_1∧⋯∧e_n.
Remark 2.35 in the integer multiplicity case: ∫_W|β_j| ≤ M_W(T_j) and |Dβ_j|(W) = M_W(∂T_j).
BV compactness (Simon Ch. 2, 2.6) and a diagonal a.e. subsequence give β_{j′} → β in L¹_loc with β integer valued.
T = τ({β≠0}, |β|, sign(β)e_1∧⋯∧e_n); at Lebesgue points the tangent space is ℝⁿ by iwl_weighted_tangent_locality.
